A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMU/CLIP-MoE research. Their complete text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. Analyses presented in v1's main text can be matched to v3's appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP-MoE retrieval, classification, LLaVA, ablation, and routing results, including Tables 1-4.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds individual-expert MMVP evaluations and additional LLaVA benchmark results in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: Both versions use multistage contrastive learning to extract FFN experts, initialize the same sparse MoE architecture, and train routers with contrastive and load-balancing losses while freezing other parameters. The revised exposition introduces no procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: The LLaVA evaluation expands from five benchmarks in v1 Table 2 to ten in v3 Table 3, adding MM-Vet, VizWiz, MMStar, OCRBench, and GQA. This broadens evaluation data and coverage, including blind-user visual questions and dedicated OCR testing. Training datasets and retrieval/classification coverage remain unchanged; MMVP already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: Direct Fine-Tuning, Sparse Upcycling, and Long-CLIP retain their corresponding retrieval/classification comparisons. The LLaVA comparator remains OpenAI CLIP, and CLIP-Recap remains in the efficiency comparison, now in Appendix A.2. The individual-expert study is an internal analysis rather than a new baseline against CLIP-MoE.

E3.justification: v3 adds a protocol evaluating each of four experts separately across nine MMVP attributes. Existing training settings, retrieval splits, and LLaVA training procedures remain as stated in v1. The changed scores for retained MLLM benchmarks are not accompanied by an explicit protocol revision.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct quantitative investigation of expert specialization across nine MMVP attributes (Table 1), extending the mechanistic evidence beyond v1's stage ablation, routing frequencies, and selected examples. The existing two-expert ablation is retained under a revised label; routing analysis and case studies move to the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional result entries do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds expert-level MMVP results and five MLLM benchmark columns, while revising retained LLaVA scores. For example, the first pair's TextVQA values change from 58.2/58.8 to 46.1/46.8, without an explanation establishing a comparable-setting gain or loss. Retrieval and individual classification scores remain unchanged. Classification averages and efficiency-comparison R@10 entries are removed.

T1.justification: The accumulated-cluster definition, MCL objective, routing equations, and load-balancing formulation are mathematically unchanged. v1's Equations (1)-(5) are split and renumbered as v3's Equations (1)-(9); no new proof, assumption, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 drops v1's explicit claim to be the first approach introducing sparsely activated MoE into CLIP foundation models. The central claims of model-agnostic DMU, inexpensive expert construction, and improved downstream representations remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds attribute-specific interpretations of expert specialization and suggests larger LLMs better exploit CLIP-MoE's visual information. It also qualifies classification gains more explicitly. The modality, scaling, and generative-text limitations largely restate v1's future-work discussion rather than introduce new boundaries.

D1.justification: The release statement changes from 'codes and models' to code, while new Appendix A.4 states that no pretrained models are released and adds licensing/reuse statements. v3 also removes explicit 7B/13B labels from the LLaVA table. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, memory, and training-time disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds benchmark references and cites He et al. (2024) when arguing that copied experts are overly homogeneous. Citations to Cumo and Eagle disappear alongside the earlier priority positioning. These are localized changes within the retained contrastive-learning and MoE research framing.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introductory, related-work, baseline, and interpretation passages are rewritten or condensed. Discussion material is reorganized into the evaluation and appendix, future work becomes a separate Limitations section, and unfinished placeholders are removed.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, adds the specialization table, substantially restructures the LLaVA table, and relocates the case-study and routing figures to the appendix with exchanged numbering. Classification-average and efficiency R@10 columns disappear, and retrieval-table winner highlighting is corrected. The LLaVA table loses model-size labels.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 provides more direct evidence for expert specialization and broader downstream validation, while removing unfinished prose. These additions modestly strengthen empirical support and readability. Benefits are partly offset by unexplained revisions to existing LLaVA scores, missing model-size labels, and the narrower model-release statement, which weaken traceability and reproducibility documentation.
